name: level2-playthrough-bankruptcy
description: Level 2 (Grumpstone Ridge) bankruptcy scenario: buy a management office, a five-vehicle fleet and a ten-strong crew, blast nothing, collapse. `campaign start level:grumpstone_ridge` fails outright (tier-2, locked by default on a fresh campaign) -- the run continues against the substitute new_game world instead, same class as the already-documented level3-playthrough-ecology.json/treranium_depths issue; see Finding #58. That is why the funding cheat is on `new_game` here rather than on `campaign start`. The run is funded to exactly the shopping list ($185,800), so every purchase is a click a real player could make and the spree ends on exactly $0 -- under the $5,000 BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD from the first tick, with BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS = 100 ticks of payroll and upkeep and no income finishing the job. The named bankruptcy outcome is unchanged and still real: levelEndReason:'bankruptcy' fires at tick 100, reported by the tick-105 step.

steps.description: cash:185800 sits on `new_game`, not on the `campaign start` below, because that `campaign start` fails outright -- grumpstone_ridge is tier-2 and locked on a fresh campaign (see the file description and Finding #58), so it never replaces this state and a `cash:` on it would be thrown away with the rest of the command. The figure is deliberately exact -- $8,000 management office + $165,000 of vehicles (rock_digger $50,000 + debris_hauler $25,000 + drill_rig $35,000 + building_destroyer $30,000 + a second debris_hauler $25,000) + $12,800 of hires -- so the overspend this scenario is about happens on enabled buttons and lands the player on exactly $0, with nothing left over to postpone the collapse.
No `cash:` here on purpose: this command fails (tier-2 level, locked on a fresh campaign), so the run continues on the new_game world above and any override attached here would be discarded with it.

Payroll and upkeep against zero income do the killing now, which is a truer test than an overdraw no player could perform.

expect.note: Finding #58: `campaign start level:grumpstone_ridge` fails outright ('Level "grumpstone_ridge" is locked. Complete previous levels first.') on a fresh campaign -- `createCampaignState()` only unlocks difficulty-tier-1 levels by default, and grumpstone_ridge is tier 2. `ctx.state` stays whatever `new_game seed:2277 cash:185800` alone produced (64x64x64 desert_badlands), never grumpstone_ridge's actual grid/biome/economics -- which is also why the funding cheat has to sit on `new_game` here rather than on `campaign start`. Same class as the already-documented, already-merged `level3-playthrough-ecology.json`/`treranium_depths` finding (PR #497) -- not fixed here either, for the same reason: properly unlocking a level is a scenario-design decision, not a drive-by. 6 of the file's 7 `build` commands (`office`/`storage_depot`/`medical_bay`/`canteen`/`break_room`/`bunkhouse`) name building types that don't exist -- only `management_office` is real ($8,000) -- matching the established Finding #5/#47 no-op pattern, correctly left unmarked already by the #479 conversion pass. All 5 vehicle purchases and all 10 employee hires used to be command-only, because cash went negative on the very first vehicle purchase and never recovered, so every real Buy/Hire button after it was disabled -- the Finding #1/#16/#46 affordability-guard class. ▸ 2026-08-08 (console funds guard, commit ddb88b3): the console now refuses a purchase the player cannot afford, so this file no longer reaches its state by overdrawing. The run is funded to exactly its shopping list ($185,800 = $8,000 office + $165,000 of vehicles + $12,800 of hires), so all 15 of those steps are now `role: 'player'` clicks on enabled controls and land the player on exactly $0 -- no headroom to postpone anything. One cosmetic discrepancy worth noting, not fixing: the `finances` command's own text prints 'Bankrupt: YES' the instant cash goes negative (a simple `cash<0` check), well before the structured `state.bankrupt` flag actually flips true -- that flag (and `levelEndReason`) requires `Bankruptcy.ts`'s real `BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100` consecutive ticks below `BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD=5000`, which is what every `expect.equals` here asserts against, never the text. The named outcome is otherwise completely real and un-dramatic to verify: cash never recovers from tick 0 onward (10 employees with zero work, zero income, draining payroll every cycle), so bankruptcy is guaranteed once the grace period elapses -- fires for real at tick 105 (`[tick 100] BANKRUPTCY! The mine is seized.`), stays true through the rest of the file's 180-tick budget. wellBeing and safety both climb toward their ceiling despite the collapse, same non-neglect mechanic as Findings #43/#44 (no blasting happens anywhere in this file, so none of the 10 hires is ever dispatched into harm). The bankruptcy tick did not move: BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD is $5,000, the spree ends on $0, so the run is under the threshold from the first tick exactly as it was when it overdrew, and BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS = 100 still expires at tick 100. Verified in both command mode and a real browser, 74/74 steps, 0 failures.
